title: Johnnycakes with Maple Syrup
subtitle: Rhode Island cornmeal griddle cakes with butter and warm syrup.
description: Cornmeal johnnycakes griddled golden and stacked with butter and maple syrup. Old-school Northeast hall breakfast — simple and satisfying.

ingredients.name: whipped butter
ingredients.notes: plus optional bacon on the side

steps.title: Scald the cornmeal
steps.instruction: Pour boiling water over cornmeal in a large bowl, whisking until smooth. Cover and rest 10 minutes so cornmeal fully hydrates and the batter thickens to porridge consistency.

steps.title: Finish the batter
steps.instruction: Whisk in milk, eggs, melted butter, sugar, and salt until uniform. Batter should pour like thick cream—thin with a tablespoon of milk if it stands in a mound.

steps.title: Heat the griddle
steps.instruction: Heat a griddle or cast iron over medium until a drop of water dances and evaporates in 2 seconds (roughly 375°F surface). Brush lightly with butter.

steps.title: Griddle the cakes
steps.instruction: Pour 1/4 cup batter per cake, spreading slightly if needed. Cook 3–4 minutes until edges look dry and bottoms are deep golden, then flip and cook 2–3 minutes more. Hold warm on a rack.

steps.title: Serve with syrup
steps.instruction: Stack three cakes per plate with whipped butter and warm maple syrup on the side. Serve immediately while edges stay lacy and centers are tender.

stationWorkflow: Scald cornmeal properly—under-hydrated batter tastes gritty and cracks on the griddle.
Cook in batches of six so the griddle stays at temp between pours.
Hold finished cakes on a rack in a 200°F oven, never stacked, to preserve crisp edges.
cleanupNotes: Wipe the griddle while still warm with a damp cloth before cornmeal hardens.
Soak mixing bowls immediately—cornmeal batter dries into cement quickly.
leftovers: Reheat cakes on a dry griddle over medium until edges re-crisp, about 2 minutes per side.
Crumble stale johnnycakes into cornbread stuffing for a dinner side later in the week.

adaptable.note: Use oat, almond, or soy milk (check tree-nut/soy status of the substitute). Use a plant-based butter/margarine.
